verdict.label: HOLD — Iran Deal Signal Clears Oil Trigger; FOMC June 17 Is the New Fulcrum
verdict.rationale_short: Trump cancelled planned Iran strikes and signaled that VP Vance will sign a peace agreement in Europe this weekend, sending Brent down 6.2% to $89.52 — clearing the framework's primary BEARISH trigger. SPX rallied 1.8% to ~7,395 and the semiconductor complex surged ~8% despite a dramatically hot May PPI (+1.1% m/m vs +0.7% consensus). The morning STEP ASIDE call was wrong directionally. Regime is materially improving — Brent and DXY both cleared, VIX compressing toward 18 — but SPX is still 65 pts below the 7,460 floor, 30Y remains pinned at ~5.00% on the hot PPI, and the Iran signing has not yet been formally confirmed. HOLD: do not chase the 1.8% rip. The next binary is the Iran deal weekend confirmation (signed → SPX likely clears 7,460 at Monday open, verdict upgrades to BUY) versus the June 17 FOMC (if Warsh signals higher-for-longer on PPI 6.5% + CPI 4.2%, 30Y spikes and creates a tactical pullback).

bear_case: May PPI +1.1% m/m is the hottest goods inflation reading since December 2009. The morning brief's own rule mandated a STEP ASIDE → BEARISH conversion at ≥0.8% m/m; the conversion was forestalled only by Trump's Iran deal signal — a signal with no binding commitment and a signing ceremony that depends on the Ayatollah not withdrawing final approval. If the weekend signing collapses (as the April 21 ceasefire did), Brent snaps back toward $95 within hours, DXY re-breaches 100, and the BEARISH verdict activates at Monday's open. Separately, the Warsh FOMC on June 17 must navigate CPI 4.2% + PPI 6.5% without any dovish cover from oil — the 30Y at 5.00% is incompatible with the SPX reclaiming 7,460 on a sustained basis; history shows SPX struggles to maintain valuation multiples above 22x forward earnings with the 30Y above 4.90%. ADBE's CFO departure is a tail risk for software sector sentiment, as institutional investors may interpret it as signal of internal disagreement over the AI strategy pivot. Invalidation: if Iran deal is formally signed over the weekend with a Hormuz reopening commitment, Brent falls to $82-86, 30Y retreats to 4.70%, and SPX closes above 7,460 for two consecutive sessions — HOLD converts to BUY.
